narrative: The model’s output is a 15% estimated chance that you will fail the final year. That is a low fail probability: it implies roughly an 85% chance of passing. On the information supplied, it does not support saying you are predicted to fail or are obliged to take remedial courses; the school would need to explain any separate rule. The strongest influence on the estimate was your reason for choosing the school—reputation—which was associated with a lower fail risk and is the choice for about 29% of students who passed. Second was your past class failures, which are zero, matching the passing-group average and lowering risk. Third was family relationship quality, rated good, as it was for about 62% of students who passed. All three pushed the estimate toward passing, not failing. Your zero absences versus an average of 3.78 among passed students also points to lower risk. To improve further, keep attending consistently, maintain your two-to-five hours of weekly study, and use family support and home internet for regular revision. If remedial courses are still required, ask for the specific evidence behind that requirement, because the model’s 15% fail probability points toward passing.
